In [[proof theory]], a branch of [[mathematical logic]], '''proof mining''' (or '''proof unwinding''') is a research program that studies or analyzes formalized proofs, especially in [[mathematical analysis|analysis]], to obtain explicit bounds, [[linear logic|ranges]] or [[rate of convergence|rates of convergence]] from proofs that, when expressed in natural language, appear to be [[nonconstructive proof|nonconstructive]].<ref>
{{cite book
| title = Applied Proof Theory: Proof Interpretations and Their Use in Mathematics
| url = https://archive.org/details/appliedprooftheo00kohl
| url-access = limited
| author = Ulrich Kohlenbach
| author-link = Ulrich Kohlenbach
| publisher =  Springer Verlag, Berlin
| year = 2008
| pages = [https://archive.org/details/appliedprooftheo00kohl/page/n18 1]&ndash;536}}
</ref>
This research has led to improved results in analysis obtained from the analysis of classical proofs.
